rationale: The assistant correctly named the anti-crease phase at turn two but then invented a 10-15 minute limit and, when told it runs about an hour (normal for Beko anti-crease), pivoted to a door-switch/control-board fault using inverted logic - the drum stopping when the door opens actually proves the switch works. It never suggested the obvious step of checking the manual for the anti-crease setting or simply unloading promptly, repeated the model-number request and near-identical door-switch paragraph, pushed a multimeter continuity test, and ended by recommending an engineer to replace a part for a non-fault. Safety instructions (unplug first) were fine, but the homeowner would be sent to pay for an unnecessary repair on a 3-month-old dryer under warranty.
